title: What Martí Wrote: Reporting in the Past

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know reported speech with *dijo que* and *afirmó que* from B1 Unit 13: *decir*, *afirmar* or *explicar* + *que*, and when the reporting verb is in the past the verb inside moves back. The present becomes the imperfect, the preterite becomes the pluperfect, and the future becomes the conditional. History is told this way: you say that someone wrote, or said, or explained something. In this lesson every report is a paraphrase in your own words, never a quotation.

sections.title: Tense shifts in reports
rows: Martí escribió: quiero la independencia. -> Martí escribió que quería la independencia.
present -> imperfect: he wrote that he wanted independence
Carlos: Martí publicó el ensayo en 1891. -> Carlos dijo que Martí había publicado el ensayo en 1891.
preterite -> pluperfect: Carlos said that Martí had published the essay in 1891
Meg: visitaré Viñales. -> Meg dijo que visitaría Viñales.
future -> conditional: Meg said that she would visit Viñales
La guía: los mogotes son colinas. -> La guía dijo que los mogotes eran colinas.
present -> imperfect: the guide said that the mogotes were hills

items.spanish: Martí escribió que quería la independencia de Cuba.
items.english: Martí wrote that he wanted the independence of Cuba.

items.spanish: Carlos dijo que Martí había muerto en 1895.
items.english: Carlos said that Martí had died in 1895.

items.spanish: Martí explicó que su deber era impedir que Estados Unidos se extendiera por las Antillas.
items.english: Martí explained that his duty was to stop the United States from spreading across the Antilles.

items.spanish: La guía dijo que los mogotes eran colinas de roca caliza.
items.english: The guide said that the mogotes were limestone hills.

sections.content: The shift happens only when the reporting verb is in the past. *Martí dice que quiere* (present) keeps the present, but *Martí dijo que quería* moves back. Pronouns and time words move too: *aquí* becomes *allí*, *mañana* becomes *al día siguiente*. And never put words in an author's mouth: when you do not have the exact words, report the idea with *explicó que*.
